chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said: Ismail ibn Sa'd al-Ahwas narrated to me, saying: I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him):
How many rak'at are in the prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Fifty-one rak'at. Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa — similar to it.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are in the daily prayers according to Imam al-Rida (as)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) specifies the total number of rak'at in daily obligatory prayers as fifty-one, a count that includes the Sunnah prayers alongside the Fard units. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the precise numerical structure of daily worship, distinguishing it from the Sunni count of thirty-nine rak'at. The placement in Al-Kafi under optional prayers highlights the importance of these additional units in completing the daily devotional routine.
